final_candidate.name: soft_span_dif_confinement
final_candidate.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis (empirical proxy, no fitted constants): if the adsorbate heavy-atom enclosing radius SPAN grows relative to the framework included-along-free-path sphere lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif), the adsorbate samples a more confining local pore space, and the reported confinement mechanism (smaller pore space => larger rotational entropy loss, E02; translational + rotational losses both contribute, E03) implies the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R increases, equivalently Sads/Sgas decreases. The descriptor is a bounded soft ratio, not a physical size-equality threshold: q-ratio forms do not preserve native equality of SPAN and lsd_p.
final_candidate.rationale: SPAN is a heavy-atom, implicit-H enclosing radius about the center of mass; it is a coarse proxy for the rotational exclusion radius of the guest and is not the full all-atom molecular geometry. lsd_p (Dif) is the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path, NOT the bottleneck Df and NOT necessarily the global cavity diameter Di that the FER/FAU rotational-entropy comparison (E02) used; the mapping from Dif to 'cavity confinement' is an explicit proxy assumption. AV is deliberately NOT used: it is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility and cannot be read as molecule-specific free volume. Legitimate SPAN zeros (single-site rotor cases, n=54) are preserved natively: descriptor = 0 there, with no median imputation. The saturating form keeps the descriptor finite over the whole training support and encodes the empirical expectation that once the guest is much larger than the pore space, additional guest size changes little (weak additional confinement signal), while changes in lsd_p at fixed guest size remain informative.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: Falsified if, holding lsd_p fixed, empirically measured entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R decreases or is invariant as SPAN increases within training quantiles [0, 1]; or if the apparent dependence is confounded by accessible-volume effects (AV/ASA co-varying with lsd_p), indicating the descriptor is a stand-in for translational accessibility rather than the proposed rotational confinement mechanism; or if substituting lsd_f (the passing bottleneck Df) for lsd_p changes the sign/strength of the relation, showing Dif was not carrying the confinement signal.
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes: (1) heavy-atom SPAN is an acceptable exclusion-radius proxy for rotational freedom of the guest, noting linear molecules are represented by the same heavy-atom span; (2) Dif (included-along-path sphere) is an acceptable proxy for the local confining pore space that drives rotational entropy loss, acknowledging it is neither the passing bottleneck Df nor the global cavity diameter used in the source comparison; (3) adsorption regime is compatible with the source conditions (zeolite adsorption at unresolved temperature/loading) and the transfer to this benchmark remains a hypothesis; (4) no source percentage, coefficient, or fitted value is imported as a universal constant. These are assumptions, not established causality.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite on the full training support: q_SPAN and q_lsd_p are nonnegative and lsd_p has no zeros in training (min 3.3452 angstrom), so the denominator q_SPAN + q_lsd_p > 0 everywhere. Legitimate SPAN zeros (54 single-site cases) map to descriptor value 0 and are preserved as physical zeros, not imputed. Descriptor is bounded in [0, 1): it saturates toward 1 for SPAN >> lsd_p and is monotone increasing in SPAN and decreasing in lsd_p.

To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. draft.name: soft_span_dif_confinement
draft.hypothesis: Conditional physical hypothesis (empirical proxy, no fitted constants): if the adsorbate heavy-atom enclosing radius SPAN grows relative to the framework included-along-free-path sphere lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif), the adsorbate samples a more confining local pore space, and the reported confinement mechanism (smaller pore space => larger rotational entropy loss, E02; translational + rotational losses both contribute, E03) implies the entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R increases, equivalently Sads/Sgas decreases. The descriptor is a bounded soft ratio, not a physical size-equality threshold: q-ratio forms do not preserve native equality of SPAN and lsd_p.
draft.rationale: SPAN is a heavy-atom, implicit-H enclosing radius about the center of mass; it is a coarse proxy for the rotational exclusion radius of the guest and is not the full all-atom molecular geometry. lsd_p (Dif) is the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path, NOT the bottleneck Df and NOT necessarily the global cavity diameter Di that the FER/FAU rotational-entropy comparison (E02) used; the mapping from Dif to 'cavity confinement' is an explicit proxy assumption. AV is deliberately NOT used: it is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility and cannot be read as molecule-specific free volume. Legitimate SPAN zeros (single-site rotor cases, n=54) are preserved natively: descriptor = 0 there, with no median imputation. The saturating form keeps the descriptor finite over the whole training support and encodes the empirical expectation that once the guest is much larger than the pore space, additional guest size changes little (weak additional confinement signal), while changes in lsd_p at fixed guest size remain informative.
draft.falsification_criteria: Falsified if, holding lsd_p fixed, empirically measured entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R decreases or is invariant as SPAN increases within training quantiles [0, 1]; or if the apparent dependence is confounded by accessible-volume effects (AV/ASA co-varying with lsd_p), indicating the descriptor is a stand-in for translational accessibility rather than the proposed rotational confinement mechanism; or if substituting lsd_f (the passing bottleneck Df) for lsd_p changes the sign/strength of the relation, showing Dif was not carrying the confinement signal.

Known proxy limitations: (1) Df is a passing bottleneck, NOT the global cavity diameter Di cited in the FER/FAU comparison (E02); the mapping from cavity confinement to bottleneck confinement is a hypothesis, not an established equivalence. (2) GeDi is computed in the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, so it can underestimate the all-atom extension relevant to a fixed geometric probe. (3) Legitimate zero values of GeDi (single-site/linear rotor branches, 54 training zeros) are preserved; q_GeDi is undefined at GeDi=0, so the descriptor must be evaluated within explicit rotor_case branches rather than median-imputed. (4) Both lengths enter as q-normalized values, so the bounded ratio is an empirical ordering device, not a physical overlap criterion.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, holding lsd_f fixed, entropy loss does not increase with native GeDi across the training GeDi quantile range, or if predictive performance is equivalent to that of q_GeDi or q_lsd_f alone (i.e., the ratio adds no ordering information beyond its factors), or if the observed relation runs in the opposite direction (larger GeDi/Df ratio associated with smaller loss), which would indicate the bottleneck plays no confinement role in this regime and that another mechanism (e.g., energetics or framework chemistry not captured by geometry) dominates.
descriptor_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes bottleneck passage restricts adsorbate translational mobility in proportion to the GeDi/lsd_f ratio; assumes heavy-atom GeDi is an adequate length-scale proxy for the all-atom molecule; assumes Df (passing bottleneck) transfers the cavity-confinement mechanism reported for FER vs FAU (E02) even though Df is geometrically distinct from average cavity diameter; assumes infinite-dilution, rigid-framework conditions not resolved in the source excerpts. These are working proxy assumptions, not established causality.
descriptor_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: GeDi in [0, 10.97181443] angstrom (54 legitimate zeros, preserved; no median imputation), lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom (no zeros). Descriptor is bounded in (0, 1) where defined; at GeDi=0 within applicable rotor branches the q-ratio is undefined rather than physically zero, so evaluation must respect rotor_case branching.

In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. The translational and rotational partition functions are available in the usual statistical mechanics texts $ ^{44,45} $ but are ultimately unimportant for the derivation that follows. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Novel topology-based, data-driven approaches have been shown to be adequate in predicting specific features such as adsorption capacity $ ^{6} $ and selectivity. $ ^{26} $ However, there are currently no similar models for entropy.

review_issues.explanation: Name/formula mismatch: the slot name 'bottleneck_pair_span_ratio' references 'span', but the formula uses q_GeDi (heavy-atom maximum pair distance), not SPAN (heavy-atom enclosing radius about the center of mass). SPAN is a distinct input with a different definition and its own 54 training zeros. The label does not identify the variable actually used; if the name is taken literally as SPAN, the record is mislabeled; if GeDi is intended, the name is misleading for downstream provenance.

The execution_check is status='rejected' with reason 'Wrong physical variable mapping: lsd_f requires bottleneck_free_sphere_Df', but the draft's variable_mappings already declare lsd_f as 'bottleneck_free_sphere_Df (framework)', which exactly matches the input definition in inputs.lsd_f. The stated rejection ground does not correspond to any identifiable mapping error in the draft as submitted. The discrepancy between the rejection reason and the draft content is unresolved; scientific_consistency remains 'unverified' and mechanism_validated is false, so the draft cannot be treated as scientifically validated regardless of whether the rejection reason is spurious.

Incorrect claim about q_GeDi at GeDi=0. Under the stated normalization q_X = X/X_ref with X_ref > 0 (GeDi_ref = 3.302656784), q_GeDi is defined and equals 0 at GeDi=0; the descriptor then evaluates to 0/(0 + q_lsd_f) = 0, a finite value. The draft's rationale and boundary_behavior claim 'q_GeDi is undefined at GeDi=0' and 'bounded in (0, 1)'; the actual defined range over native inputs is [0, 1). Consistently, expression_check uses regime_train_quantiles [0.0, 1.0], which includes the zero point the draft calls undefined — an internal inconsistency. rotor_case branching may remain scientifically advisable for the underlying physics, but it is not required for definitional validity of this formula, and the stated undefinedness/median-imputation motivation is inaccurate.

Imprecise attribution of GeDi zeros: the draft attributes the 54 legitimate zeros to 'single-site/linear rotor branches', but zero_n = 54 for GeDi exactly matches the single_site rotor count (54), while the linear branch (214 members) has nonzero largest-pair distances. The zeros arise from the single-site (single-atom) branch only; the 'linear' attribution is unsupported by the training statistics.

Proxy mapping from bottleneck to cavity confinement is a hypothesis, correctly flagged but not independently supported. E02's reported mechanism concerns the average cavity diameter (FER ~4.3 Å vs FAU ~13 Å) as the confinement descriptor; lsd_f is Zeo++ Df, the largest sphere that can pass through a periodic free path — a geometrically distinct quantity from average cavity diameter Di. The knowledge graph permits lsd_f as a proxy only under MAY_USE_PROXY_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS edges (conditional), and no edge establishes equivalence between Df and Di. The draft acknowledges this, but the record should retain that the Df→cavity-confinement transfer is unverified; it is not established by the cited source.

Mechanism-family inconsistency: mechanism_family is declared 'translation', but the primary cited confinement evidence (E02) concerns rotational entropy loss, and the draft's own hypothesis text leads with the rotational-loss mechanism. The link 'bottleneck passage restricts translational mobility in proportion to GeDi/lsd_f' is an added assumption not stated in E02; E03 only reports that both translational and rotational losses contribute, without attributing either to bottleneck geometry. The directional prediction (loss increasing with GeDi at fixed lsd_f) is internally consistent with the formula's monotonicity, but its mechanistic support mixes a rotational-loss source with a translational proxy assumption.

The limit test (lsd_f → positive_infinity, expected value 0.0) is mathematically correct for the ratio form but lies far outside the training support of lsd_f ([0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom, max 7.68726). The limiting regime is extrapolative with no training data; it validates only the algebraic limiting behavior, not behavior in the empirically supported domain.

Non-duplication relative to the round-1 appended descriptor (q_SPAN)/(q_SPAN + q_lsd_p) is satisfied — both numerator (q_GeDi vs q_SPAN) and denominator (q_lsd_f vs q_lsd_p) differ — but this holds only if GeDi (not SPAN) is the intended variable. Given the 'span' string in the slot name (see name/formula mismatch above), duplicate-screening provenance is ambiguous until the naming inconsistency is resolved. This issue is recorded as a provenance risk, not as a detected duplicate.

In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. The translational and rotational partition functions are available in the usual statistical mechanics texts $ ^{44,45} $ but are ultimately unimportant for the derivation that follows. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. draft.rationale: Round 1 used the adsorbate enclosing radius SPAN against the included-along-path sphere lsd_p. This descriptor is a distinct, non-duplicate combination: it pairs the heavy-atom maximum pair distance GeDi (a length-scale proxy for the molecule's largest extension) with the passing bottleneck Df (the largest free sphere that can traverse a periodic path), probing confinement of translational motion through channel restrictions. Known proxy limitations: (1) Df is a passing bottleneck, NOT the global cavity diameter Di cited in the FER/FAU comparison (E02); the mapping from cavity confinement to bottleneck confinement is a hypothesis, not an established equivalence. (2) GeDi is computed in the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation, so it can underestimate the all-atom extension relevant to a fixed geometric probe. (3) Legitimate zero values of GeDi (single-site/linear rotor branches, 54 training zeros) are preserved; q_GeDi is undefined at GeDi=0, so the descriptor must be evaluated within explicit rotor_case branches rather than median-imputed. (4) Both lengths enter as q-normalized values, so the bounded ratio is an empirical ordering device, not a physical overlap criterion.

review_issues.explanation: Name/formula mismatch: the slot name 'bottleneck_pair_span_ratio' references 'span', but the formula uses q_GeDi (heavy-atom maximum pair distance), not SPAN (heavy-atom enclosing radius about the center of mass). SPAN is a distinct input with a different definition and its own 54 training zeros. The label does not identify the variable actually used; if the name is taken literally as SPAN, the record is mislabeled; if GeDi is intended, the name is misleading for downstream provenance.

The execution_check is status='rejected' with reason 'Wrong physical variable mapping: lsd_f requires bottleneck_free_sphere_Df', but the draft's variable_mappings already declare lsd_f as 'bottleneck_free_sphere_Df (framework)', which exactly matches the input definition in inputs.lsd_f. The stated rejection ground does not correspond to any identifiable mapping error in the draft as submitted. The discrepancy between the rejection reason and the draft content is unresolved; scientific_consistency remains 'unverified' and mechanism_validated is false, so the draft cannot be treated as scientifically validated regardless of whether the rejection reason is spurious.

Incorrect claim about q_GeDi at GeDi=0. Under the stated normalization q_X = X/X_ref with X_ref > 0 (GeDi_ref = 3.302656784), q_GeDi is defined and equals 0 at GeDi=0; the descriptor then evaluates to 0/(0 + q_lsd_f) = 0, a finite value. The draft's rationale and boundary_behavior claim 'q_GeDi is undefined at GeDi=0' and 'bounded in (0, 1)'; the actual defined range over native inputs is [0, 1). Consistently, expression_check uses regime_train_quantiles [0.0, 1.0], which includes the zero point the draft calls undefined — an internal inconsistency. rotor_case branching may remain scientifically advisable for the underlying physics, but it is not required for definitional validity of this formula, and the stated undefinedness/median-imputation motivation is inaccurate.

Imprecise attribution of GeDi zeros: the draft attributes the 54 legitimate zeros to 'single-site/linear rotor branches', but zero_n = 54 for GeDi exactly matches the single_site rotor count (54), while the linear branch (214 members) has nonzero largest-pair distances. The zeros arise from the single-site (single-atom) branch only; the 'linear' attribution is unsupported by the training statistics.

Proxy mapping from bottleneck to cavity confinement is a hypothesis, correctly flagged but not independently supported. E02's reported mechanism concerns the average cavity diameter (FER ~4.3 Å vs FAU ~13 Å) as the confinement descriptor; lsd_f is Zeo++ Df, the largest sphere that can pass through a periodic free path — a geometrically distinct quantity from average cavity diameter Di. The knowledge graph permits lsd_f as a proxy only under MAY_USE_PROXY_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS edges (conditional), and no edge establishes equivalence between Df and Di. The draft acknowledges this, but the record should retain that the Df→cavity-confinement transfer is unverified; it is not established by the cited source.

Mechanism-family inconsistency: mechanism_family is declared 'translation', but the primary cited confinement evidence (E02) concerns rotational entropy loss, and the draft's own hypothesis text leads with the rotational-loss mechanism. The link 'bottleneck passage restricts translational mobility in proportion to GeDi/lsd_f' is an added assumption not stated in E02; E03 only reports that both translational and rotational losses contribute, without attributing either to bottleneck geometry. The directional prediction (loss increasing with GeDi at fixed lsd_f) is internally consistent with the formula's monotonicity, but its mechanistic support mixes a rotational-loss source with a translational proxy assumption.

The limit test (lsd_f → positive_infinity, expected value 0.0) is mathematically correct for the ratio form but lies far outside the training support of lsd_f ([0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom, max 7.68726). The limiting regime is extrapolative with no training data; it validates only the algebraic limiting behavior, not behavior in the empirically supported domain.

Non-duplication relative to the round-1 appended descriptor (q_SPAN)/(q_SPAN + q_lsd_p) is satisfied — both numerator (q_GeDi vs q_SPAN) and denominator (q_lsd_f vs q_lsd_p) differ — but this holds only if GeDi (not SPAN) is the intended variable. Given the 'span' string in the slot name (see name/formula mismatch above), duplicate-screening provenance is ambiguous until the naming inconsistency is resolved. This issue is recorded as a provenance risk, not as a detected duplicate.

In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. AV is deliberately NOT used: it is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility and cannot be read as molecule-specific free volume. Legitimate SPAN zeros (single-site rotor cases, n=54) are preserved natively: descriptor = 0 there, with no median imputation. The saturating form keeps the descriptor finite over the whole training support and encodes the empirical expectation that once the guest is much larger than the pore space, additional guest size changes little (weak additional confinement signal), while changes in lsd_p at fixed guest size remain informative.
appended.falsification_criteria: Falsified if, holding lsd_p fixed, empirically measured entropy loss (Sgas - Sads)/R decreases or is invariant as SPAN increases within training quantiles [0, 1]; or if the apparent dependence is confounded by accessible-volume effects (AV/ASA co-varying with lsd_p), indicating the descriptor is a stand-in for translational accessibility rather than the proposed rotational confinement mechanism; or if substituting lsd_f (the passing bottleneck Df) for lsd_p changes the sign/strength of the relation, showing Dif was not carrying the confinement signal.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes: (1) heavy-atom SPAN is an acceptable exclusion-radius proxy for rotational freedom of the guest, noting linear molecules are represented by the same heavy-atom span; (2) Dif (included-along-path sphere) is an acceptable proxy for the local confining pore space that drives rotational entropy loss, acknowledging it is neither the passing bottleneck Df nor the global cavity diameter used in the source comparison; (3) adsorption regime is compatible with the source conditions (zeolite adsorption at unresolved temperature/loading) and the transfer to this benchmark remains a hypothesis; (4) no source percentage, coefficient, or fitted value is imported as a universal constant. These are assumptions, not established causality.
appended.boundary_behavior: Finite on the full training support: q_SPAN and q_lsd_p are nonnegative and lsd_p has no zeros in training (min 3.3452 angstrom), so the denominator q_SPAN + q_lsd_p > 0 everywhere. Legitimate SPAN zeros (54 single-site cases) map to descriptor value 0 and are preserved as physical zeros, not imputed. Descriptor is bounded in [0, 1): it saturates toward 1 for SPAN >> lsd_p and is monotone increasing in SPAN and decreasing in lsd_p.
